title: Transaction deadline closes the connection before rollback
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a setup that runs out of time rolls back over the open connection before it closes' (VAL-111), 'a rollback that fails at the deadline is reported next to the timeout', 'a rollback that never finishes cannot hold the setup past its hard cap', 'a rollback already under way when the deadline passes is not cut off', 'setup work still running when the deadline passes sends nothing while the rollback runs', 'a mutation still unanswered when the rollback begins is rolled back', 'a mutation whose snapshot is still being read when the rollback begins is never sent'
proof: Holds. The transactionTimeout timer in withObsConnection called done() directly: it settled the connection, rejected every pending request, closed the socket and resolved the caller with the plain timeout message, so configureObsStream's finish (and with it transaction.rollback()) never ran over a live connection; a callback rejection that reached finish afterwards sent its restores into a settled connection. The tests run configureObsStream against a fake OBS socket (through a new optional connectionOptions seam that passes timeouts to withObsConnection) that logs every request and the close. On the unchanged code the VAL-111 test failed: log was GetStreamStatus, GetStreamServiceSettings, SetStreamServiceSettings:whip_custom, close, where the restore SetStreamServiceSettings:rtmp_custom was expected before close, and the result message was the bare 'OBS setup timed out after 50ms.' with no rollback status. The other six failed for the same reason (no restore before close, no rollback status in the message, a rollback already under way cut off at the deadline with the timeout message instead of its own result, and a dispatched but unanswered mutation not replayed by a rollback that begins before its answer or timeout). Fix: withObsConnection passes its callback a third argument { signal, onDeadline }; at the deadline, a callback that registered a handler gets the signal aborted and the handler called with the timeout result, and a hard cap (deadlineGraceMs, default 18.7 s = 10 x 250 ms stop gate + 1.2 s video settle + 3 request timeouts) closes the connection and settles with 'OBS setup timed out after Nms. Rollback incomplete: not finished <grace>ms later, so the connection was closed.' if the handler has not settled; without a handler the deadline settles at once as before; openObsControlChannel (Infinity deadline) is untouched. configureObsStream registers onDeadline(finish) so the deadline takes the same path as any other failure: rollback over the open connection, then done, with 'OBS settings were restored.' appended when the rollback was clean ('Rollback incomplete: ...' otherwise); a finish already under way is not restarted or cut off at the deadline (only the hard cap bounds it). Because a timed-out setup is stuck inside a request, createObsConfigurationTransaction now tracks mutations that were sent and not yet answered and a rollback replays them as it does a timed-out one (a StopStream is excluded, as for a timeout), and refuses to send a mutation whose snapshot read finished after the rollback began. The housekeeping stream test (releaseStaleEncoder) is sent through a channel that rejects once the deadline signal is aborted, so it cannot interleave with the rollback.
